In the medieval Kingdom of Portugal , the Cortes was an assembly of representatives of the estates of the realm – the nobility , clergy and commoners .  It was called and dismissed by the King of Portugal at will, at a place of his choosing. [ 1 ] Cortes which brought all three estates together are sometimes distinguished as Cortes-Gerais (General Courts), in contrast to smaller assemblies which brought only one or two estates, to negotiate a specific point relevant only to them. [ 2 ]
